brief.summary: Lodging and visitor-logistics software for biological field stations, handling bunk assignments, meal counts, boat and vehicle transfers, and arrival paperwork for visiting researchers and courses, with built-in guidance for station staff who are new to it.
brief.user: Tomás Arguedas, three weeks into his job as assistant station manager at the Río Sierpe Biological Station, a university-run research station on Costa Rica's Osa Peninsula. He has hospitality experience from an eco-lodge but has never used this system, and the station manager who trained him is away at a conference until next week.
brief.moment: A 22-person tropical ecology field course from a U.S. university arrives by boat in two days, overlapping with three independent researchers already in residence. Tomás is trying to turn the course's provisional 'block hold' into confirmed bunk assignments and he doesn't understand several things the system is telling him: what the difference between a 'block hold' and a 'tentative' booking means for the meal counts the kitchen already received, why four students show 'waiver incomplete' and whether that stops check-in, and why one cabin is flagged 'restricted – permit housing'. He needs to learn just enough to finish the assignments and send the kitchen and boat captain correct numbers today without breaking anything.
brief.data: Station capacity: 6 cabins (Heliconia, Ceiba, Manglar, Tucán, Garza, Researcher House), 58 bunks total, each with sleeps-count, bathroom type and gender-designation rules. Current residents: 3 researchers (Dr. Ana Pazos, 41-night stay; 2 grad students on a frog-call project). Incoming: 'BIO 377 Tropical Field Ecology' block hold of 24 bunks, Nov 18–Dec 2, 20 students + 2 instructors listed, 2 unnamed slots; 4 students with waiver status 'incomplete', 1 with dietary note 'celiac'. Meal plan: 3 meals/day, kitchen currently has 27 covers per meal for Nov 18. Boat transfer from Sierpe dock Nov 18 at 13:30, capacity 14 per trip, 2 trips needed. Manglar cabin flagged 'restricted – permit housing' for MINAE permit inspectors Nov 25–27. System terms Tomás hasn't learned: block hold, tentative, release date (block hold releases unconfirmed bunks Nov 17 at 17:00), cover count, waiver gate. Help content and short how-to articles exist for each of these.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.
